verses.text: If someone is called in public to tell what he knows as a witness, and he saw or knew something but does not speak up, he has sinned and must carry the blame.

Or someone may touch something unclean, like the dead body of an unclean wild animal, an unclean farm animal, or an unclean crawling creature. Even if he did not notice it, he has become unclean and is guilty.
Or he may touch something unclean from a person, anything at all that makes someone unclean. Even if he did not notice it, when he finds out, he is guilty.
Or someone may carelessly make a promise to do something, bad or good, the kind of careless promise people make, and not realise it. When he finds out, he is guilty in this matter.
When someone is guilty in any of these ways, he must admit the sin he has done.
Then he must bring the LORD his offering for the sin he has done: a female lamb or goat from the flock, as a sin offering. The priest will make him right with God for his sin.
If he cannot afford a lamb, he must bring the LORD two doves or two young pigeons for the sin he has done: one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
He will bring them to the priest, who will first offer the bird for the sin offering. He will twist its neck, but not pull the head right off.
He will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood will be drained out at the bottom of the altar. It is a sin offering.
Then he will offer the second bird as a burnt offering, in the way that has been commanded. In this way the priest will make him right with God for the sin he has done, and he will be forgiven.

But if he cannot afford two doves or two young pigeons, he must bring about one and a half kilograms of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put oil or incense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He will bring it to the priest, and the priest will take a handful of it as the part that is remembered and burn it on the altar, on top of the gifts made by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
In this way the priest will make him right with God for any of these sins he has done, and he will be forgiven. The rest of the flour will belong to the priest, just like the grain offering."

"If someone is unfaithful and sins without meaning to against the LORD's holy things, he must bring the LORD a guilt offering: a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it. Its value is set in silver, by the official weight used at the holy place.

He must pay back what he has done wrong about the holy thing, and add one fifth more, and give it to the priest. The priest will make him right with God with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If someone sins by doing something the LORD has commanded must not be done, even if he did not know it, he is still guilty and must carry the blame.

He must bring the priest a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it, of the set value, as a guilt offering. The priest will make him right with God for the wrong he did without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He was truly guilty before the LORD."
